title: nudge: subtask progress does not hide a stuck implementer; guard follow-ups from #60
goal: Close issues #152 and #60. (1) `factory-pipeline.py nudge` reported a stuck implementer start prompt as ok because a sibling subtask's commit on the same task branch counted as task progress (plan none-affected-notrun, about 58 minutes lost). (2) The process and git guard misses `cmd //c` (the Git Bash form), several kill forms, flags the recommended own-PID pattern, and some quoted-text negative tests run where the old guard never checked processes, so they prove nothing.

tasks.objective: Issue #152. In scripts/factory-pipeline.py `cmd_nudge` (around line 5655) the per-terminal check calls `task_progress_since(plan, reg, t, since)` (around line 5065), which counts any new commit on the task branch, the lead report, or any review/QA verdict of the task or its subtasks. For a spec of the implement phase (spec file name `<task>-implement-<digest>.md`, or however `orca_prompt` names implement specs: read it), task-level progress must not clear a terminal: the lead commits subtask work and sibling implementers report, so neither proves this session started. For such a spec count only progress that belongs to this spec's own dispatch: a verdict or worker record of the subtask whose implement spec this is, when the spec can be mapped to a subtask (check what dispatch records next to the spec, e.g. the model record or the subplan); when it cannot be mapped, no progress counts and the screen pointer plus idle time decide. Lead, verify and other phase specs keep today's task-level rule. Keep `nudge` read-only apart from the one keystroke and its record, keep the never-twice rule, keep the composer-line pointer rule of PR #148. Add tests in tests/pipeline.test.sh with the existing fake `orca`: two implementer terminals in one task worktree with two implement specs, a commit on the task branch after both specs, one terminal still showing its composer pointer and idle -> STUCK (and sent once with --send), the other terminal whose pointer is gone -> ok; a lead-phase terminal with a commit after its spec stays ok (unchanged rule). Changelog fragment changelog.d/nudge-subtask-progress.md (### Fixed).
acceptance: an idle implementer terminal that still shows its spec pointer on a composer line is STUCK although a sibling subtask committed to the task branch after its spec was written
lead and verify terminals keep the task-level progress rule
every existing pipeline nudge case passes

tasks.objective: Issue #60 (read it: `gh issue view 60`). The guard is advisory only. (1) scripts/lib/rpgf_guard/shell.py `expand()` (the `if p in CMDS:` branch around line 236) accepts `/c` and `/k` but not the Git Bash forms `//c` and `//k`: accept them, so `cmd //c "taskkill /F /IM dotnet.exe"` gets the process advisory and `cmd //c "git push --force origin main"` gets the force-push advisory. Update the wrapper list in the scripts/lib/gitguard.py docstring. (2) scripts/lib/rpgf_guard/process.py: flag `Get-Process <name> | % Kill`, `| ForEach-Object Kill`, `| ForEach-Object -MemberName Kill` (and `.Kill()` on a name-selected Get-Process), `pkill.exe`, `busybox killall`/`busybox pkill`, `killall5`, and kills by port (`fuser -k`, `kill $(lsof -t ...)`, `kill $(lsof -ti:PORT)`). Keep quoted text as data (no new false positive on grep/echo/commit message text). EncodedCommand stays a documented limitation. (3) False positive: a command that starts a process, queries processes by name, and kills only the PID it started must not be flagged: `./run.sh & pid=$!; pgrep -f run.sh; kill $pid` and `$p = Start-Process dotnet -PassThru; Get-Process dotnet; Stop-Process -Id $p.Id`. Exempt a terminator whose only targets are variables assigned from `$!` or from a `-PassThru` Start-Process result in the same command; a terminator fed by a name query (`kill $(pgrep x)`, `taskkill //PID $(... Win32_Process ...)`) stays flagged. (4) tests/git-guard.test.sh: add cases for every item above (positive and negative), and move several of the quoted-text negative process cases (around line 281-299, currently run with `$TMP`) to the `$SERVER` working directory so they would fail on a guard that flagged quoted text inside the workspace. Every new bypass class also gets a case in tests/installed-safety.sh if that suite covers process or wrapper classes (check it). Changelog fragment changelog.d/guard-followups.md (### Fixed).
acceptance: `cmd //c` and `cmd //k` are expanded like `/c` and `/k` for both the git rules and the process rule
the kill forms listed in #60 item 2 get the process advisory; quoted mentions of them stay quiet
the two own-PID examples of #60 item 3 get no advisory; a kill fed by a name query still does
several quoted-text negative process cases run in the $SERVER working directory
every existing git-guard and installed-safety case passes
